old: The Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF) won a decisive victory. Historian József Antall formed a center-right coalition government, pledging to serve as 'Prime Minister of 15 million Hungarians in spirit'. The Parliament elected 1956 veteran Árpád Göncz as President, sealing the peaceful birth of the democratic third Republic.
new: The Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF) won the most seats. József Antall formed a coalition government with two smaller parties and said he wished to be 'Prime Minister of 15 million Hungarians in spirit'. In August the Parliament elected the writer Árpád Göncz, a 1956 prisoner, as President of the Republic.
why: 'decisive victory', 'center-right', 'sealing the peaceful birth of the third Republic' are labels/judgements

old: Consensus and Political Negotiation: megállapodnak abban, hogy...
new: Agreeing and Negotiating: megállapodtak, hogy ...

old: Formulas of Multi-Party Deliberation
new: Recap: hogy clauses, plus negotiation phrases

old: Describing negotiated transitions uses verbs of multilateral accord: *megállapodnak abban, hogy...* ('agree on the fact that...'), *tárgyalóasztalhoz ül* ('sits down at the negotiating table'), *kompromisszumos megállapodást köt* ('strikes a compromise agreement').
new: You know *hogy* clauses from A2 Unit 11 and *hogy* + a verb in *-jon/-jen* from B1 Unit 5. Together they say what the sides agreed: *megállapodtak, hogy az átmenet békés legyen* ('they agreed that the transition should be peaceful'). Phrases for the talks: *tárgyalóasztalhoz ül* ('sits down at the negotiating table'), *kompromisszumot köt* ('strikes a compromise'), *közös nevezőre jut* ('reaches common ground').
why: taught cataphoric abban, hogy (B2) and known hogy clauses as new

old: The parties of the Opposition Roundtable agreed to act unitedly during the negotiations.
new: The organisations of the Opposition Roundtable agreed to act together in the negotiations.

old: The National Roundtable secured the legal framework for the peaceful transition.
new: At the National Roundtable, representatives of the ruling party and the opposition sat down at one table.

old: Decisive Historical Turning Points: utat nyit vmi előtt, lebont
new: Words and Phrases for the Border Opening of 1989
why: 'decisive turning points' is a judgement; no grammar is taught

old: Metaphors of Opening and Demolition
new: Phrases for the events of 1989

old: Key historical idioms: *utat nyit a szabadság előtt* ('opens the way to freedom'), *lebontja a vasfüggönyt* ('dismantles the Iron Curtain'), *áttöri a határt* ('breaks through the border').
new: Useful phrases for 1989: *lebontja a szögesdrótot* ('takes down the barbed wire'), *megnyitja a határt* ('opens the border'), *menedéket kér* ('asks for shelter'), *átlépi a határt* ('crosses the border'). You know *előtt* from A1 Unit 18: *megnyitja a határt a menekültek előtt* ('opens the border to the refugees').

old: The Hungarian border opening opened the path toward the reunification of Germany and Europe.
new: After the border opening many East Germans left for the West.

old: At the Pan-European Picnic, hundreds of East German families crossed over into Austria.
new: During the Pan-European Picnic about six hundred East Germans crossed into Austria.

old: On June 16, 1989, three hundred thousand people paid tribute before the coffins of Imre Nagy and his companions at Heroes' Square.
new: On 16 June 1989 about three hundred thousand people paid tribute before the coffins of Imre Nagy and his companions at Heroes' Square.

old: In the speech, they firmly demanded the immediate withdrawal of occupying Soviet troops from Hungary.
new: In the speech they demanded the withdrawal of the Soviet troops from Hungary.

old: Following the spring 1990 elections, the first free government was formed under the leadership of József Antall.
new: After the spring 1990 elections the first freely elected government was formed under the leadership of József Antall.

old: Lakitelek gathering (September 1987 birth of the democratic opposition)
new: Lakitelek, the village where the MDF was formed in September 1987
why: the democratic opposition began earlier; Lakitelek was the founding of the MDF

old: Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF, leading center-right opposition party)
new: Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF, formed at Lakitelek in 1987, later a party)

old: European reunification triggered by Hungarian border opening
new: Berlin Wall (opened on 9 November 1989)

old: Pan-European Picnic (August 19, 1989 peace demonstration near Sopron)
new: Pan-European Picnic (19 August 1989, a demonstration near Sopron during which about 600 East Germans crossed into Austria)

old: withdrawal of Soviet occupation forces from Hungarian territory
new: withdrawal (of troops); the last Soviet soldier left in June 1991

old: moral and political rehabilitation of the executed 1956 heroes
new: martyr; here the executed leaders of the 1956 revolution

old: historical justice delivered through public remembrance
new: historical justice, i.e. public acknowledgement of the injustice done to the victims

old: Heroes' Square (scene of the 300,000-strong historic memorial service)
new: Heroes' Square (where the ceremony of 16 June 1989 took place, with an estimated 250,000-300,000 people)

old: October 23rd (connecting 1956 revolution with the 1989 free Republic)
new: 23 October (the anniversary of the 1956 revolution, and the day the Republic was proclaimed in 1989)

old: comprehensive constitutional amendment replacing socialist tenets
new: constitutional amendment (in force from 23 October 1989)

old: first democratically elected Prime Minister
new: first Prime Minister after the free elections of 1990

old: 1956 prisoner elected first President of the Republic
new: writer and 1956 prisoner, elected President of the Republic by Parliament in August 1990
why: he was not the first president of any republic of Hungary

old: center-right coalition government led by MDF, FKgP, and KDNP
new: coalition government of the MDF, the FKgP and the KDNP (May 1990)

old: regime change / complete transformation of Hungary's political order
new: change of regime (the political transformation of 1989-1990)

set.english: The Hungarian change of regime took place peacefully, by negotiation.
The Antall government was formed in May 1990.
